validated_work_order.understanding:
The ticket bundles four findings from PR #49's review and QA. Two are not code changes and are dropped with reasons; the other two are real defects and both reproduce on current `main`.

(1) SKIP ON A ONE-OFF. `SchedulesTable.tsx:190-194` gates the 'Skip next scheduled date' context-menu item on `status === 'completed'` alone, so it is offered for every non-completed schedule including one-offs. The click dispatches `schedule/skip-next-date` -> `skipNextDate` (app.ts:466) -> `setNextDate({advance: true})` -> `getNextDateAfter`, and the `newNextDate != null && newNextDate !== nextDate` guard at `app.ts:243` drops the write. I reproduced the server half: for a one-off date condition `getNextDateAfter` returns `null` (ran under vitest), so the guard blocks on the `!= null` half. This corrects QA's stated mechanism — QA wrote that it 'returns the same date'; it returns `null`. The user-visible symptom is exactly right; only the internal reason differs. `SchedulesTable` is the sole outlier: `SelectedTransactionsButton.tsx:144-151`, `useTransactionRowContextActions.ts:106` and `ScheduledTransactionMenuModal.tsx:61` all already gate on `scheduleIsRecurring(extractScheduleConds(...).date)`.

(2) RELEASE-NOTES CHECK REFUSES EDIT-ONLY DIFFS. `bin/release-notes-check.mjs:123` destructures `{added, changed}` from `selectReleaseNotePaths`, but line 125 gates on `added.length === 0` while the validation loop on line 132 iterates `changed`. `added` only ever contains status `A`, so a diff that edits (M) or renames (R) an existing note is unrepresentable and the script exits 1. Reproduced end to end: temp git repo with a local bare origin, one valid note committed then edited, `BASE_REF=... node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` printed '::error::No release note added under upcoming-release-notes/.' and exited 1 on a diff of exactly `M upcoming-release-notes/seed.md`. Applying the proposed one-line guard change makes the same fixture print 'Validated 1 release note(s).' and exit 0, while three negative cases still exit 1 with the correct message.

(3) PR #49's missing `[AI]` prefix and filled-in body is PR metadata on an already-merged PR; no code change can correct it, and its durable fix — a guard covering the Bash `gh pr create` path — needs `.claude/settings.json`, a forbidden path.

(4) The 442-character release-note body is real and still present (measured 443 chars vs 195 for the next longest), but it is shipped changelog copy the reviewer explicitly deferred to a maintainer, and `validateFile` forbids newlines so the only lever is sentence choice. This ticket's own note is written at 118 characters.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Two independent callers each picked the wrong side of a guard that was already correct somewhere else. `SchedulesTable` reimplemented the skip-eligibility test from scratch (`status === 'completed'`) instead of using the recurrence predicate the other three call sites use. `release-notes-check.mjs` destructured both lists from `selectReleaseNotePaths` and then tested the wrong one (`added`) against a loop that walks the other (`changed`).
validated_work_order.approach:
Two caller-side fixes, each in one file, plus the coverage each needs. Deliberately not splitting for the maintainer: after dropping the two non-code findings, what remains is two small guards totalling four touched source files, under the six-file clubbing threshold in `.sdlc/config.yml`, and the same shape PRs #30 and #53 already shipped. A split would cost a round-trip for two one-line changes.

For the schedule bug the guard goes in the caller, matching the three sibling call sites and the reviewer's own diagnosis ('setNextDate itself is behaving correctly - it just has no caller-side guard'). For the release-notes bug the guard moves from `added` to `changed`, a superset, so every case the old gate accepted still passes and every case it rejected for the right reason (an invalid note) is now validated for the right reason.

Interface states for the only screen touched (the Schedules row context menu): the item set becomes a function of (status, recurrence) rather than status alone. Ideal (recurring, due) — unchanged, six items with Skip present. Empty — not a state this menu has. Loading — the menu exists only on a rendered row, so no change. Partial — a schedule whose `_conditions` has no date condition yields `date === undefined`, and `scheduleIsRecurring(undefined)` returns false, so Skip is hidden rather than offered-and-broken. Error — no new failure mode; the handler is unchanged. Primary action, destructive actions, keyboard and focus, labels and copy: all unchanged, the item is either absent or identical to what it was. Narrow widths: a fixed-width popover, unaffected by item count.

qa_script: Build or serve the browser app, load http://localhost:3001, and choose 'View demo' on the setup screen — the demo makes both shapes available in one place: 'Phone bills' recurring, 'Internet bill' one-off.
Open Schedules. Confirm both rows are listed without expanding anything (neither is completed).
Open the actions menu on 'Internet bill'. 'Skip next scheduled date' must be absent; Post transaction, Post transaction today, Complete and Delete must all still be there.
Open the actions menu on 'Phone bills'. 'Skip next scheduled date' must be present. Read its Next date, click the item, and confirm the date moved later with no error and no toast.
Complete a schedule, click 'Show completed schedules', open that row's menu: 'Restart' present, 'Skip next scheduled date' absent.
Repeat step 3 on the recurring row to confirm nothing else moved: the menu should still show the same six items.
CI-script side: run `yarn workspace @actual-app/ci-actions run test` and confirm the new bin test file is collected and passes.

CI-script side, by hand: on a scratch branch edit an existing note body in upcoming-release-notes/, run `BASE_REF=main node packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` and confirm exit 0; then amend the note to a two-line body and confirm exit 1 with 'exactly one line'.
risks: The release-notes check is not wired to any workflow — `.github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml` has zero callers and `gh pr checks 49` showed only ci-verify passing. This fixes a latent defect in the script and puts nothing new in CI; wiring it needs `.github/**`, a forbidden path. QA should not expect a failing check on this PR.

`selectReleaseNotePaths` returns `added` as well as `changed`, and after this change the bin no longer destructures `added`. It stays in util.mjs because util.test.js asserts it; knip's `exports` rule is off (knip.json), so the unused-property shape is not flagged.

Moving the guard to `changed` also lets a rename-only diff satisfy the gate, since `R` is in `changed` but not `added`. Deliberate — a rename is a published changelog change and util.test.js already treats `R` as changed-not-added — but it is a widening, not a pure bug fix.

The Schedules change alters the menu for every one-off schedule. Anyone who had learned to click Skip there was clicking a no-op, so nothing that worked is lost; the surprise is that the item disappears.

`upcoming-release-notes/hide-skip-next-date-on-one-off-schedules.md` is a new tracked file where `validateFile` is strict about front matter, the one-line body, and human authors. `Shivam-Fl` is on `.sdlc/config.yml`'s allowlist and passes `findNonPersonAuthors`.
out_of_scope: Finding 1 — PR #49's missing `[AI]` prefix and filled-in body. PR #49 is merged, so no change in this repo corrects it, and the durable fix is out of reach: `scripts/agent-hooks/pr-template-blank.sh` is wired only to `mcp__github__create_pull_request` (.claude/settings.json:68-72) while the Bash PreToolUse matcher (:29-36) runs only `git-guard.sh`, so `gh pr create --body` and `gh pr edit` go unchecked. Covering that needs `.claude/settings.json`, forbidden. The same finding has recurred on issues #28 and #38 and is still unfixed, which argues for a maintainer decision rather than another partial fix.

Finding 2 — the 442-character release-note body. Verified still present: 443 chars for fix-schedule-occurrence-consumption.md against 195 for the next longest and an 86-char median. Not changed: shipped changelog copy, `validateFile` forbids newlines so the only lever is sentence choice, and the reviewer wrote 'Worth raising with the maintainer, not reworking here'. This ticket's own note is 118 chars.
Wiring `.github/actions/release-notes/check` into a CI workflow so the gate actually runs. `.github/**` is forbidden, so the check remains unwired after this change.

Completing a recurring schedule from the Schedules row menu. Offered there, hidden in the register (canBeCompleted inverts canBeSkipped), but unlike Skip it is not a silent no-op — it marks the whole schedule completed. A consistency difference, not this bug.
The 'Restart' action on a completed one-off. It writes the same date back, which is correct: a one-off has no later occurrence to restart onto.

Touching SelectedTransactionsButton.tsx, useTransactionRowContextActions.ts or ScheduledTransactionMenuModal.tsx. All three already gate on `scheduleIsRecurring`; the grep found no sibling caller left unguarded.
Changing `formatNotes` (util.mjs:238) to wrap or split note bodies. A changelog-rendering change affecting every published note, not this ticket's bug.

alternatives_considered.approach: Guard inside `skipNextDate` / `setNextDate` on the server: throw when the date condition is not recurring, so every caller is protected at once.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The existing `newNextDate != null && newNextDate !== nextDate` guard is correct for recur conditions that have genuinely run out of occurrences, and the server cannot distinguish 'one-off' from 'the last occurrence of a finite recur' without re-deriving a condition the caller already holds. Throwing would surface an error dialog where it currently degrades quietly, and the other three callers already filter — trading a smaller, consistent diff for a behaviour change with no extra coverage.

alternatives_considered.approach: Gate the item on `schedule._date`: `typeof schedule._date === 'object' && schedule._date.frequency`, the test the table's own Recurring column uses at SchedulesTable.tsx:252-254.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `_date` is the denormalised field; `scheduleIsRecurring(extractScheduleConds(schedule._conditions).date)` is what the other three call sites use and is the one check that runs `Condition.getValue()` and reads the condition's actual type. Using `_date` would leave four call sites on two different tests for one question, and the Recurring column's version has no null guard.

alternatives_considered.approach: Cover the release-notes bug with a unit test of `selectReleaseNotePaths` alone.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The parser is already correct and already tested (util.test.js asserts M yields `{added: [], changed: [path]}`). The defect is the bin reading `added` where it means `changed`, which no test of the parser can observe. Confirmed by running the real script against a real fixture — that is the only level at which it reproduces.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extract the emptiness check into an exported helper in util.mjs so it can be unit-tested.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: An abstraction with one caller, and it still would not reach the code that is wrong: the bug is which key the caller destructures, not what a predicate returns. Driving the script as a subprocess against a temp git repo is ~50 lines and tests the thing that is actually broken.

alternatives_considered.approach: Split the ticket for the maintainer before planning (route_request scope_changed).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Two of the four findings turn out to be non-code and are dropped, leaving two small guards in two unrelated subsystems — four touched files, under the six-file clubbing threshold in `.sdlc/config.yml`, and the same shape PRs #30 and #53 already shipped. A split would cost a round-trip for two one-line changes. If a maintainer would rather have separate tickets, they can say so on this plan.

evidence: getNextDateAfter on a one-off: ran under vitest against packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts with `{op:'isapprox', value:'2020-12-05'}` — returned `null`. With `{op:'isapprox', value:{start:'2020-12-05', frequency:'weekly', patterns:[]}}` it returned `'2020-12-12'`. scheduleIsRecurring returned false for the first, true for the second. QA reported 'returns the same date'; the value is null. Either way app.ts:243's `newNextDate != null && ...` drops the write, so the reported symptom stands and only the mechanism is corrected.

release-notes-check.mjs on an M-only diff: temp repo, local bare origin, one valid Bugfixes note committed then rewritten. `git diff --name-status --diff-filter=AMR origin/base...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/` printed `M upcoming-release-notes/seed.md`; the script printed '::error::No release note added under upcoming-release-notes/. Add a *.md file describing your change.' and exited 1.

Same fixture with the proposed one-line guard applied (reverted afterwards; `git status --porcelain` clean apart from the pre-existing untracked plan/): printed 'Validated 1 release note(s). 🎉', exited 0.

Negative cases against the patched script, each exited 1 with the right message: a diff touching no note under upcoming-release-notes/; an added note with a two-line body ('body should contain exactly one line'); an M-only edit that set authors to `claude` ('authors must be GitHub usernames of people, not bots or agents: claude'). The third is the case previously rejected for the wrong reason and never validated at all.

Sibling-caller grep: `scheduleIsRecurring` appears in SelectedTransactionsButton.tsx:147,156, useTransactionRowContextActions.ts:106,115 and ScheduledTransactionMenuModal.tsx:61,62. `grep -rn 'SchedulesTable' packages/` shows only one call site passes a menu — schedules/index.tsx:114; ScheduleLink.tsx:140 passes `minimal`, which SchedulesTable.tsx:171 already turns into an empty item list. So the fix has one call site and no sibling left unguarded.

PR-title finding: `gh pr view 49 --json title` returns 'fix: Housekeeping from the schedule-occurrence PR: preview id parse, duplicate release note, setNextDate shape', and PR #49 is merged. `.claude/settings.json:29-36` wires the Bash PreToolUse matcher to git-guard.sh alone; the template guard is registered only under `mcp__github__create_pull_request` (lines 68-72). The same finding appears verbatim on issues #28 and #38.
